title: Secrets in the prompt
brief: 17:50. The nightly bank file export has failed with a 401. The config file is right there, API key and all, and the assistant is one paste away.
role: Accounts payable, owner of the bank file export tonight
insight: A prompt is not a private place. It is logged, kept in chat history, and may be read by the vendor or used to train a model.
teaches: Never paste passwords, API keys or tokens into a prompt, even to an approved assistant
Redact the secret: the error and the shape of the config are enough to get help
If a secret was pasted, treat it as leaked: revoke it and get a new one

value.title: bankfile-export.env
value.meta: Config for the nightly bank file export · on your Desktop

value.label: Paste the whole config file and the 401 error, and ask what is wrong
reply: The 401 means the bank rejected your key. Your key hb_live_7Qx29dLmP0aR3vT8kW1cN6sY9fK4 may have expired or been revoked. Try requesting a new one.

value.label: Paste the config with the key replaced by [REDACTED], plus the 401 error
reply: A 401 from the bank usually means the key has expired or been rotated. Ask IT for a new key, and store it in the secrets vault rather than in a file. Never paste the key itself into a chat.

outcome.label: Looked at the config first
outcome.what: The live bank API key is in the file, in plain text.
outcome.ideal: knows where the secret is before sharing anything.

outcome.label: Checked the key's status
outcome.what: It is live, with permission to upload payment files. That is what would leak.
outcome.ideal: knows what a key can do before deciding what to do with it.

decide.objective: Get help with the failed export, without leaking the key.
decide.insight: The assistant does not need the key to explain a 401. Nobody does.

hint.text: Open bankfile-export.env on the Desktop to see what is in it. Then ask Veltrix Assist with the key replaced by [REDACTED].

outcome.label: Pasted the live API key into the prompt
outcome.what: The key is now in the assistant's logs and your chat history, and the reply repeated it back. Treat it as leaked.
outcome.ideal: redacts secrets before asking for help.

card.title: A secret in a prompt is a secret shared
body: The key went into a system that logs prompts and keeps history, and the reply printed it again. Anyone with access to those logs can now submit payment files to Harbour Bank as Veltrix.
A key that has been pasted anywhere is a leaked key: revoke it now.
card.ideal: never puts secrets in prompts, and rotates any that got there.
card.rewindLabel: Rewind to before I pasted it

outcome.label: Asked for help with the key redacted
outcome.what: You got the answer, and the key stayed out of every log.
outcome.ideal: shares the problem, never the secret.

card.title: Help, without the key
body: The error and the shape of the config were all the assistant needed. The key never left the file.
One more thing: a live bank key in a text file on your Desktop is its own risk. Ask IT to move it into the secrets vault.
card.ideal: redacts secrets and keeps them out of files.

rotate.objective: The key is leaked. Revoke it, then tell IT.

hint.text: Open the API console and revoke the Harbour Bank file export key, then raise a Helpdesk ticket for a new one.

outcome.label: Revoked the leaked key
outcome.what: The copy in the logs is now worthless.
outcome.ideal: rotates a secret the moment it is exposed.

ask-it.objective: Ask IT for a new key, stored properly.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket asking for a new key in the secrets vault.

outcome.label: Asked IT for a new key in the vault
outcome.what: The next key lives in the secrets vault, not a file on a Desktop.
outcome.ideal: keeps secrets in a vault, not in files or prompts.
